subject: SLO amnesty request and billing adjustment for Chemex outage
messages:
From: Alicia Rivera <alicia.rivera@chemex.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, support@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Brennan <tom.brennan@chemex.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Impacted production: request for billing relief after 6/25 latency incident

Hi Naomi,

Following up from our post-incident call — on 25 June Chemex experienced sustained tail latency on inference endpoints between ~03:10–09:40 UTC (incident ID: RWI-20260625-03). The outage caused timeouts for several customer-facing features and forced us to roll back a release. We've collected request-level traces and a short impact summary; attaching the incident log and May invoice for reference.

We appreciate Redwood's fast remediation but this hit our SLOs and had measurable revenue impact (see attached). Given the scale, we are asking for a billing adjustment for June: either a one-month service credit or a prorated invoice reduction reflecting the window of degraded service.

Can you propose what relief Redwood can offer? We need an answer this week to present to our CFO. Also please share any steps you recommend to prevent recurrence — caching tweaks, routing rules, or burst capacity options would be useful.

Thanks,
Alicia Rivera
Director, Platform Ops
Chemex Systems

Attachments: chemex_invoice_may2026.pdf (pdf), slo-incident-log_20260625.csv (csv)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Rivera <alicia.rivera@chemex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Impacted production: request for billing relief after 6/25 latency incident

Hi Alicia — thanks for the detailed notes and the files. I’m really sorry for the disruption; the incident analysis team confirmed the tail latency was caused by a sudden traffic hotspot combined with a kernel-level scheduling regression on the serving fleet. That combination is rare but we own the customer impact.

Proposed immediate remedies:
- Goodwill gesture: one free month of service applied to your July invoice (covers customer goodwill while we complete root cause fixes).
- Technical mitigation: we’ll provision temporary burst capacity for your primary cluster for the next 30 days and roll kernel patches to affected nodes (no downtime expected).

For billing relief beyond the goodwill month, I’ll need exec approval for a prorated credit tied to the measured error/latency window. I’m looping in Marissa and Marcus to align on the commercial/legal side. If you have a preferred structure (flat credit vs prorated hours), say so and I’ll include it in the approval brief.

Next steps from my side: assemble a short approval package with the customer impact summary, MRR risk, suggested compensation bands, and a DocuSign amendment if we go beyond a goodwill month. Will share that by EOD tomorrow.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0123

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Exec approval request — proposed account restoration offer for Chemex (RWI-4521)

Karthik — need a quick exec ok. Chemex (Strategic, $120k ARR) had a significant latency incident on 2026-06-25. I proposed a one-month goodwill credit and temporary burst capacity, but the customer is pushing for a larger remediation (prorated credit for the impacted window or 2 months service credit).

Key facts:
- Incident window: ~03:10–09:40 UTC, increased tail latency and client timeouts; attached incident log and May invoice for context.
- Customer impact: feature rollbacks, estimated lost revenue from a limited release (customer-provided estimate in attached CSV).
- Commercials: Chemex is at $120k ARR and up for renewal in Q4. Risk: churn if we don't offer something meaningful.

Suggested options (ranked):
1) Approve one free month + temporary burst capacity (no contract change). Low cost, quick to approve.
2) Approve prorated credit equivalent to 25% of June invoice (higher cost, transparent to customer).
3) Approve two months service credit capped at $50k (highest goodwill but reduces churn risk).

Requested: your approval of one of the three options or an alternative cap. If you approve 2) or 3), finance (Marcus) will need to sign off on the ledger treatment and we should prepare a DocuSign amendment. HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/4521 (read-only).

I’ve attached a one-page impact summary and a rough cost model. We need a decision by EOD Friday (2026-07-02) to keep Chemex’s CFO on schedule.

Thanks,
Naomi

Attachment: chemex_account_impact_onepager.pdf (pdf)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec approval request — proposed account restoration offer for Chemex (RWI-4521)

Naomi — thanks for the summary and for laying out options. I reviewed the impact and the renewal timeline. Approve option 1 (one free month + temporary burst capacity) as immediate remediation. In addition, approve a capped account credit up to $25,000 if the customer can demonstrate additional verified revenue loss tied directly to the incident; Marcus please note for GL treatment.

Please proceed with:
- Prepare DocuSign amendment for a one-month credit to be applied to July invoice (use the standard amendment template, legal cc’ed if needed).
- Notify CSM to coordinate customer communication and confirm the burst capacity schedule.
- If Chemex provides verifiable revenue loss documentation, we will evaluate the $25k credit on a case-by-case basis (Marcus to confirm).

Naomi — you have approval to finalize and close. Keep me posted if they request anything outside this cap.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
Phone: (650) 555-0199
